drug_class: RNA interference (RNAi) therapy / small interfering RNA (siRNA)
purpose: Givosiran is used to treat adults with a rare condition called acute hepatic porphyria (AHP). This disease causes sudden, severe attacks of stomach pain, weakness, and other serious symptoms. This medicine helps reduce how often those attacks happen.
how_it_works: Your body makes too much of a toxic substance in the liver that triggers porphyria attacks. Givosiran works by silencing a specific gene in your liver cells, which lowers the production of that toxic substance. Think of it like turning down the volume on a gene that is turned up way too high.
common_side_effects: Nausea, tiredness, injection site reactions (redness, pain, or swelling where the shot is given), kidney problems (noticed on blood tests), and elevated liver enzymes (noticed on blood tests).
warnings: This medicine can cause serious kidney and liver problems, so your doctor will check your kidney and liver function with regular blood tests. Tell your doctor right away if you notice swelling, decreased urination, or unusual fatigue. It is given as an injection under the skin, and injection sites should be rotated. Avoid this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant unless your doctor has carefully weighed the risks and benefits.
typical_dosing: Givosiran is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a month. The usual dose is 2.5 mg per kilogram of your body weight. It is typically given by a healthcare provider or can sometimes be self-administered after proper training.
